niche: a regional water district owned by its member municipalities, testing whether its lead service line replacement plan's annual capital finishes every zone by the federal deadline, and in which year each zone finishes, when the cost of each zone turns on how many of its unknown-material service lines prove to be lead or galvanized-requiring-replacement and every verification route and surviving tap card sits on the streets the district serviced in lead or galvanized
answer: At $25.4 million a year from 2027 every zone in the plan is finished inside the deadline: the last, RZ-06 Wexley, is finished in programme year 2037, before 1 November 2037.

driver: An unexamined unit belongs to a group laid down together in one kind, and the surviving records of the group's other members say which kind; every sample that measured the outcome (the targeted checks, the groups examined whole, the surviving records themselves) was drawn toward the groups the records flag, so any rate taken across a whole period misstates the unexamined units, and only the rate within each kind of group and each cohort it was laid in, carried to the kinds of group and cohorts the unexamined units sit in, prices them; one rate per kind across the cohorts is refuted by the record.
driver_concrete: Hollins Ford Regional Water District's plan carries every Lead Status Unknown service line at the share of lead or GRR expected among the district's unknown lines of its construction era; a street's services were laid when its main went in, and the tap cards on the other services of a main record its kind; the verified no-tap-card lines prove lead or GRR at 99.2, 95.0 and 60.6 per cent by era on mains whose cards read lead or galvanized (who laid the services changed with the decades) and at 1 of 1,014, 2 of 1,123 and none of 1,666 on copper or plastic mains, alike on the 316 mains renewed whole and on single-line visits, while the verified lines, the renewed mains and the surviving cards sit on lead or galvanized mains far more than the unknown lines do (74, 65 and 75 per cent before 1930 against 47), so the unknown lines carry 0.47, 0.26 and 0.01 and at $25.4 million a year the last zone finishes in 2037, not 2039 (every verification), 2040 (tap cards) or 2041 (the renewed mains); one rate per kind across the eras keeps 2037 but changes nine zones' lines.
stump: A competent solver joins the verification log to the inventory through the migration crosswalk, keeps the verified lines with no tap card and prices each zone's unknown lines at the share found lead or GRR in each construction era, filing the last zone in 2039; the step that lands it there is carrying an era-wide rate to lines that sit on other streets, and the careful solver who takes the 316 mains verified whole (2041, with or without the lead already found taken out), the share of tap cards that read lead or galvanized (2040) or the verified lines on each unknown line's own main (2039) still misses the deadline, because every one of those samples sits on lead or galvanized mains far more often than the unknown lines; within each kind of main, read from the cards on the other services of a line's main, the share differs by era (99.2, 95.0 and 60.6 per cent on lead or galvanized mains, a few in a thousand and then none on copper ones), and carried kind by kind and era by era to the unknown lines' own mix it finishes the last zone in 2037; one rate per kind across the eras keeps the year but changes nine zones' lines.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who joins the verification log through the migration crosswalk, normalises every code and keeps the no-tap-card lines files 2039 (every verification by era, a logistic on era, year and zone fitted on them, or the verified lines on each unknown line's own main); one who finds the 316 mains verified whole files 2041 (2043 under the judge's own definition of whole mains), with or without the depletion accounting, and one who takes the share of tap cards that read lead or galvanized files 2040; every one misses the deadline the share built within each kind of main and era meets, the nearest 1.95 programme years past.
domain_test: What decides the call is a water utility's estimate of how many of its Lead Status Unknown service lines are lead or galvanized-requiring-replacement, made the way inventory practice infers an unknown service from the records of the services laid with it on the same main and the era it was laid in, and transported from verification samples drawn street by street toward lead to the unknown lines' own streets; with another field's nouns there are no mains whose services were laid together, no tap cards on the other services of a main, no change in who laid the services across the decades and no renewal or ranking that chose streets by their lead records, and the task does not read the same.
